B) To offer products of all registered sellers in one place and help entrepreneurs build their own custom online stores without extensive technical skills or finances.
C) To provide a platform for freelancers to find jobs.
D) To offer daily deals and discounts.
questions.answer: B) To offer products of all registered sellers in one place and help entrepreneurs build their own custom online stores without extensive technical skills or finances.
questions.explanation: This particular platform offers the products of all registered sellers in one place. Web store builder allow sellers to have their own custom online store, especially for entrepreneurs without in-house resources or finances.

questions.question: In an online shopping mall or store builder, how are product listings generally priced?
options: A) Through bidding and auctions.
B) They are fixed priced.
C) Prices are determined by the mall provider based on demand.
D) Prices are negotiated directly between buyer and seller.
questions.answer: B) They are fixed priced.
questions.explanation: All listings here are fixed priced.

questions.question: Who typically provides logistics and distribution services in an online shopping mall model?
options: A) The individual sellers.
B) Third-party logistics companies chosen by the buyer.
C) The mall provider.
D) The customer is responsible for arranging logistics.
questions.answer: C) The mall provider.
questions.explanation: In general usually logistics and distribution are provided by the mall provider.

questions.question: Which of the following was mentioned as a popular example of an online shopping mall or store builder?

questions.explanation: Very popular examples are eCrater, Shopgo, Rakuten in Japan, Shopify in India.

questions.question: What defines a 'coupon business' in e-commerce?
options: A) Websites that allow individuals to sell used items.
B) Deal of the day websites featuring discounted gift certificates, which become available if a certain number of people sign up.
C) Platforms for businesses to find freelance workers.
D) Online marketplaces for B2B transactions.
questions.answer: B) Deal of the day websites featuring discounted gift certificates, which become available if a certain number of people sign up.
questions.explanation: Coupon refers to a deal of the day websites that feature discounted gift certificates usable at local or national companies. If a certain number of people sign up for the offer then the deal becomes available to all.

questions.question: How does the coupon business aim to help merchants, according to the lecture?
options: A) By providing them with a platform for auctions.
B) By helping them build a loyal customer base.
C) By offering them free advertising.
D) By connecting them with international suppliers.
questions.answer: B) By helping them build a loyal customer base.
questions.explanation: The coupon business actually helps merchants build a loyal customer base.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the minimum threshold and the discount offered in a coupon business model?
options: A) Larger the minimum threshold, smaller the discount.
B) The minimum threshold has no bearing on the discount.
C) Larger the minimum threshold, larger the discount.
D) Discounts are fixed regardless of the threshold.
questions.answer: C) Larger the minimum threshold, larger the discount.
questions.explanation: Larger the minimum threshold, larger the discount.

questions.question: What is the typical revenue model for a coupon business platform?
options: A) A fixed monthly subscription fee from merchants.
B) A portion of the amount paid by the customer for the deal.
C) Advertising revenue from third-party ads.
D) Selling customer data to other businesses.
questions.answer: B) A portion of the amount paid by the customer for the deal.
questions.explanation: The revenue model in general it is portion of the amount paid by the customer.

questions.question: Which company was cited as a global example of a coupon business?
options: A) Nearbuy
B) Rakuten
C) Groupon
D) Elance
questions.answer: C) Groupon
questions.explanation: Popular examples of e-commerce ventures that thrive on the coupon business are Groupon which is a global company.

questions.question: Why might the long-term goals of sellers (e.g., building a loyal customer base) not succeed in the coupon business model?
options: A) Customers are generally loyal to the coupon platform, not the individual merchant.
B) Customers often switch to other merchants if they find a better deal elsewhere.
C) Coupon deals are usually for products that customers only buy once.
D) Merchants cannot track customer loyalty through coupon platforms.
questions.answer: B) Customers often switch to other merchants if they find a better deal elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The problem with this is that when customers have a better deal at another company, they would switch from the first merchant to the third merchant or the second merchant.

questions.question: What is a potential negative consequence for a merchant if a coupon deal attracts a huge number of customers beyond their serving capacity?
options: A) The merchant will make more profit due to high volume.
B) The merchant might turn off a large number of customers due to poor quality of service, leading to a loss of potential loyal customers.
C) The coupon platform will charge a higher commission.
D) The deal will automatically be canceled by the platform.
questions.answer: B) The merchant might turn off a large number of customers due to poor quality of service, leading to a loss of potential loyal customers.
questions.explanation: If a huge number of customers that which is beyond the serving capacity of the merchant sign up for the deal, servicing those customers might be very difficult for the merchant. What might happen is instead of having a loyal customer base because of the poor quality of service the merchant might actually turn off a large number of customers.

questions.question: How can strong, established merchant companies pose a threat to couponing platforms?
options: A) They can offer even lower prices than the coupon platforms.
B) They can bypass the couponing platform and offer heavy discounts directly to customers, avoiding commission fees.
C) They can buy out the couponing platforms.
D) They can refuse to participate in any coupon deals.
questions.answer: B) They can bypass the couponing platform and offer heavy discounts directly to customers, avoiding commission fees.
questions.explanation: The merchant company has its own expertise in its own domain. So, it obviously, might have an upper hand compared to the couponing company. So, it can give on its own outside the couponing business it can give a heavy discount and by doing so without giving away certain commission to the couponing platform, the company can obtain a heavy the customer can obtain a heavy discount from the merchant.

questions.question: What threat do larger companies like Google or Amazon pose to the couponing business model?
options: A) They lack the technological infrastructure to run coupon deals.
B) They have a huge existing user base, and if they decide to enter the couponing business, they could be a huge threat to new entrants.
C) They are not interested in offering discounts.
D) Their business models are incompatible with couponing.
questions.answer: B) They have a huge existing user base, and if they decide to enter the couponing business, they could be a huge threat to new entrants.
questions.explanation: There are a lot of companies such as Google, Amazon which already have a huge user base. So, if they decide to come up with their own couponing business model they would since they already have a huge loyal user base they could be a huge threat to the new entrance in the couponing business.

questions.question: What is an online staffing platform or freelance marketplace primarily designed for?
options: A) Selling physical goods through auctions.
B) Connecting independent professionals (freelancers) with clients for work arrangements.
C) Providing templates for building e-commerce stores.
D) Offering daily deals and discounts on services.
questions.answer: B) Connecting independent professionals (freelancers) with clients for work arrangements.
questions.explanation: This is an online marketplace in which independent professionals and their clients can establish and fulfill work arrangements.

questions.question: What is a value proposition for clients using an online staffing platform?
options: A) They can only hire full-time employees.
B) They can post jobs, search for freelance professionals, solicit proposals, evaluate contracts, and communicate.
C) They are guaranteed to receive free services.
D) They can only work with local freelancers.
questions.answer: B) They can post jobs, search for freelance professionals, solicit proposals, evaluate contracts, and communicate.
questions.explanation: Clients allow businesses to post jobs, search for freelance professionals and solicit proposals. They also evaluate contracts and communicate.

questions.question: What information can freelancers typically post on their profile on an online staffing platform?
options: A) Only their desired salary.
B) Their past jobs, feedback, portfolio, specific skills, and educational background information.
C) Only their availability for work.
D) Their personal contact details for direct communication.
questions.answer: B) Their past jobs, feedback, portfolio, specific skills, and educational background information.
questions.explanation: The freelancers can search jobs and they can post a profile displaying their past jobs and feedback, portfolio and specific skill and their educational background information.

questions.question: What is the revenue model for an online staffing platform?
options: A) It solely relies on advertising.
B) It charges a membership fee to freelancers or clients, and/or marks up the billings of contractors by 5 to 15 percent.
C) It takes a fixed percentage of the freelancer's annual income.
D) It sells the intellectual property created by freelancers.
questions.answer: B) It charges a membership fee to freelancers or clients, and/or marks up the billings of contractors by 5 to 15 percent.
questions.explanation: The revenue model as we had discussed is a membership fee by the freelancers or it could also be a membership fee by the clients and marking up the billings of contractors or freelancers by 5 to 15 percent.

questions.question: Which of the following were mentioned as popular examples of freelance marketplaces?
options: A) Groupon and Nearbuy
B) Kickstarter and Quirky
C) Elance and oDesk
D) eBay and Priceline
questions.answer: C) Elance and oDesk
questions.explanation: Popular examples of these freelance marketplaces are Elance or oDesk.

questions.question: The lecture introduces 'unique e-commerce business models' because:
options: A) They are exclusively B2B models.
B) They are difficult to classify into traditional B2B, B2C, or C2C categories, often playing a role across multiple types.
C) They only exist in specific geographical regions.
D) They do not involve any online transactions.
questions.answer: B) They are difficult to classify into traditional B2B, B2C, or C2C categories, often playing a role across multiple types.
questions.explanation: We will now move on to unique e-commerce business models which it is very difficult to classify these business models into any of these individual domains. We cannot say that you know, it is a B2B business model or a B2C business model or a C2C business model, per say, but these business models are very-very unique pertaining specifically to the e-commerce domain and they play a role in any of these.

questions.question: Which type of e-commerce transaction is generally characterized by lower value?

B) B2C transactions
C) C2C transactions

questions.answer: B) B2C transactions
questions.explanation: B2C transactions are of low value vis a vis B2B transactions.

questions.question: What is a common practice after an auction concludes on an e-commerce platform?
options: A) The platform immediately removes the listing.
B) Buyers and sellers rate each other.
C) The platform automatically re-lists the item.
D) Only the seller provides feedback.
questions.answer: B) Buyers and sellers rate each other.
questions.explanation: After the auction buyers and sellers rate each other. This happens in any e-commerce business today.

questions.question: The video on crowdsourcing mentioned a historical example from 1714 where the British government held a contest for a solution to navigate the seas. Who answered the call and what did he invent?
options: A) John Harrison, who invented the marine chronometer.
B) Charles Babbage, who invented the analytical engine.
C) Isaac Newton, who developed the laws of motion.
D) James Watt, who improved the steam engine.
questions.answer: A) John Harrison, who invented the marine chronometer.
questions.explanation: Let us go back to 1714. Sailing the seven seas was necessary, but really dangerous to navigate. So, the British government held a contest asking people for a solution. John Harrison answered the call, he invented the marine chronometer and was awarded a large cash prize.

questions.question: Another historical example of 'relying on the crowd' mentioned in the video was the creation of the first Oxford English Dictionary. How did they achieve this?
options: A) A single scholar compiled it over decades.
B) They asked for lots of volunteers to write about different topics according to their expertise.
C) They used a government-funded research team.
D) They purchased existing dictionaries and combined them.
